(2) In any 10–digit number N = a₁a₂⋯a₁₀ the divisibility rule for 11 says that
  S = (a₁ + a₃ + a₅ + a₇ + a₉) − (a₂ + a₄ + a₆ + a₈ + a₁₀)
must be a multiple of 11 (possibly 0).

sentence: ) One may show that if one “encodes” the number by writing, for each digit d, the multiplicity c_d (with ∑₍d₌0₎⁹ c_d = 10, and not all of c₉, …, c₁ are zero) then the positions in the unique descending arrangement are completely determined, and so is the alternating sum S.

sentence: In fact one may prove that if one “marks” for each d whether c_d is even or odd then the only digits which contribute to S are those with an odd count – and their contribution comes with a plus–sign or a minus–sign depending on whether the very first occurrence of the digit falls in an “odd–position” or an “even–position” (and which is determined already by those counts for digits larger than d).
